name_en: de la Vallee Poussin error term for the prime number theorem
canonical_claim: There exists a real constant c > 0 such that, as x tends to positive infinity, the difference between the number pi(x) of primes at most x and a source-normalized logarithmic integral Li(x) is O(x * exp(-c * sqrt(log x))).
domain_and_universes: Provisional real asymptotic variable x at +infinity; Nat.primeCounting composed with a reviewed floor/nonnegative-floor convention, or an equivalent natural-variable encoding; all values in Real; conclusion in Prop; no nontrivial universes expected.
ordered_binders_provisional: the error function x |-> pi(x) - Li(x) is asymptotically Big-O at +infinity of x |-> x * exp(-c * sqrt(log x))
hypotheses_requiring_statement_freeze: the exact real or natural domain and filter
the extension of primeCounting from natural to real arguments
the definition and additive normalization of Li
the lower-domain and endpoint convention needed by log, sqrt, and the logarithmic integral
conclusion: An unconditional de la Vallee Poussin exponential-decay Big-O bound for the error pi - Li at positive infinity.

alternate_encodings.target: natural-variable sequence n |-> (Nat.primeCounting n : Real) - Li(n)
alternate_encodings.relationship: candidate equivalent restriction of the real-variable statement

alternate_encodings.target: a real-variable statement using Nat.primeCounting floor(x)
an error estimate for Chebyshev theta or psi
alternate_encodings.relationship: proof-route or transport candidate, not statement identity

degenerate_cases: Values x <= 1, x at an integer or prime jump, the singularity and normalization of Li, c = 0, a sign change in the exponent, and replacement of Big-O by little-o must be explicit statement mutations or boundaries.
